question: Train A leaves station M at 8:05 a.m. and reaches station N at 3:05 p.m. on the same day. Train B leaves station N at 10:05 a.m. and reaches station M at 3:05 p.m. on the same day. Find the time when Trains A and B meet.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total distance be the LCM of 7 hours and 5 hours = 35 units.

Speed of Train A = 35 ÷ 7 = 5 units/hr and Speed of Train B = 35 ÷ 5 = 7 units/hr.

Distance covered by A alone in 2 hours (8:05 a.m. to 10:05 a.m.) = 5 × 2 = 10 units.

Time to cover the remaining 25 units together = 25 ÷ (5 + 7) = 25/12 hours = 2 hours 5 mins.

Meeting time = 10:05 a.m. + 2 hours 5 mins = 12:10 p.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 12:10 p.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Train A starts at 8:05 a.m. and reaches at 3:05 p.m.

Train B starts at 10:05 a.m. and reaches at 3:05 p.m.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Time to meet = Remaining Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total time taken by Train A = 7 hours

⇒ Total time taken by Train B = 5 hours

⇒ Let the total distance between station M and station N be 35 units (LCM of 7 and 5).

⇒ Speed of Train A = 35 ÷ 7 = 5 units/hr.

⇒ Speed of Train B = 35 ÷ 5 = 7 units/hr.

⇒ Distance traveled by Train A in 2 hours (8:05 a.m. to 10:05 a.m.) = 5 × 2 = 10 units.

⇒ Remaining distance when Train B starts = 35 − 10 = 25 units.

⇒ Relative speed = Speed of A + Speed of B = 5 + 7 = 12 units/hr.

⇒ Time taken to meet = 25 ÷ 12 hours = 2 hours and (1/12 × 60) minutes = 2 hours 5 minutes.

⇒ Meeting time = 10:05 a.m. + 2 hours 5 minutes = 12:10 p.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 12:10 p.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Time and Speed Relationship

For a constant distance, speed is inversely proportional to the time taken (S ∝ 1/T).
